claims.text: The raw unnumbered-promo source group and the richer Asobikata slice both place the Latest Edition how-to-play route on November 13, 1998.
This unnumbered-promo source group models two raw source-index rows: Diglett 061 and Dugtrio 062.
The local unnumbered catalog states this is a source-derived campaign family grouped by a Bulbapedia promotion/distribution note, not official product-boundary proof.
The richer Asobikata evidence ties the same physical story to Japanese pre-English rows 054/055, Japanese names, Miki Tanaka credit, and later Pokemon Web e-Card reprints.
The raw unnumbered-promo rows do not provide illustrator credit, while the richer Asobikata slice records Miki Tanaka for the paired Diglett/Dugtrio object.

This bridge matters because it prevents two catalog surfaces from drifting apart: the raw index says rows 061/062, while the collector story says Asobikata Diglett and Dugtrio in a rule-teaching book.

Agents should use this group as a bridge: preserve raw indices 061/062 and the Asobikata route together, but do not treat either catalog surface as seller evidence, authenticity, condition, or spendability.

narrative.human_title: Asobikata through the raw index — when the map has two coordinates
narrative.why_it_matters: This is not a new pair of cards so much as a second coordinate system for the same little teaching object. One catalog surface says Diglett 061 and Dugtrio 062 in the raw unnumbered promo index; the richer source slice says Asobikata, Miki Tanaka, Japanese names, and the later Pokemon Web echo. The value is in keeping both maps visible, because collectors get hurt when a row number starts pretending to be the whole route.
